newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon indicts alleged killers of president - elect.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon indicts alleged killers of president - elect.

text.p: A Lebanese magistrate demanded the death penalty on Tuesday for two members of a pro-Syrian leftist group charged with planning and carrying out a bombing that killed president-elect Bashir Gemayel in 1982.

Investigating judge Sa'eed Mirza officially charged Habib Chartouni, a member of the Syrian Social National Party (SSNP), with planting and setting off the bomb and Nabil al-Alam, the SSNP's security official, of masterminding the assassination.
Both men, who are at large, will be tried in their absence by Lebanon's highest court, the Judicial Council, but no date was set. Both are Maronite Christians, like Gemayel.
Mirza had issued a warrant in 1994 for the arrest of Chartouni, who was arrested a few months after the September 14, 1982 bombing but escaped from jail in 1990.

Chartouni has said in interviews after his release that he was behind the bombing that killed Gemayel but the pro-Syrian SSNP has repeatedly said that "as a party" it had nothing to do with Gemayel's killing.

The indictment said Chartouni confessed he planted the bomb and was asked by Alam to kill Gemayel "to thwart the American designs to control Lebanon which began with the Israeli invasion (of 1982) and continued by (Gemayel's) election as president."

Gemayel formed and headed Lebanon's strongest Christian civil war militia, the Lebanese Forces (LF), and was allied with Israel when it invaded Lebanon in 1982 to crush Palestine Liberation Organisation guerrillas.
Gemayel and 23 other people died in the huge blast in an LF office in Christian east Beirut, nine days before he was due to assume office.
Chartouni was freed from jail by SSNP militiamen shortly after Syrian and Lebanese troops stormed areas controlled by rebel Christian General Michel Aoun and ousted him on October 13, 1990.
It was not clear why Chartouni was not tried in the past. The Judicial Council had opened an investigation in the 1980s into Gemayel's assassination but the outcome was not published.

Several Lebanese political leaders were assassinated in the 1975-90 civil war, including president Rene Muawad, killed in a 1989 bombing shortly after taking office, and prime minister Rashid Karami in a 1987 blast aboard an army helicopter.
Investigations have been opened into both cases but no one has been officially charged.
